sku1.headline: SKU-1 puts motor control and gate drive on one 130 nm BCD chip, for motor supplies up to 120 V.
sku1.context: A controller and gate driver usually require separate parts. SKU-1 proposes to combine those roles for motors, appliances and actuators.
sku1.implication: Choose the drive by its operating environment and required response, then assess whether integration reduces the complexity of your product.
sku1.gate: Validate the complete power stage before treating a component reduction as a production benefit.
sku1.valueTitle: One chip replaces the separate controller and gate driver.
sku1.gateTitle: The datapath is FPGA-validated at 81.25 MHz; the 120 V power stage waits for silicon.

sku2.headline: SKU-2 meters energy to Class 0.5S and keeps the tamper record on an always-on domain under 2 µW.
sku2.context: SKU-2 brings energy measurement, meter control and outage records together for utilities and meter makers.
sku2.implication: The commercial test is whether the meter meets the tender’s accuracy, tamper and service requirements.
sku2.gate: Accuracy and outage behaviour need measured evidence before a utility deployment.
sku2.valueTitle: A meter needs one chip for measurement, security and its own time base.
sku2.gateTitle: The metrology chain is FPGA-validated; Class 0.5S accuracy is not yet measured.

sku3.headline: SKU-3 makes four sequenced rails from a 28 V bus, designed for a 100 V input spike.
sku3.context: SKU-3 targets the power supplies used in military, railway and space equipment, where qualification is part of the buying decision.
sku3.implication: Select the required grade and equipment programme first; a general power-management claim is not enough.
sku3.gate: Each environmental and screening requirement must be demonstrated for the intended grade.
sku3.valueTitle: Military (883), railway (EN 50155) and space grades each run their own programme.
sku3.gateTitle: The sky130 prototype tests control logic and low-voltage rails; the 28 V stage arrives on SCL 180 nm.

sku4.headline: SKU-4 runs a checker core two cycles behind and drives FAULT_N 39 cycles after a mismatch, in simulation.
sku4.context: SKU-4 uses two processors to detect disagreement and trigger a hardware fault response. It is intended to support a system safety case.
sku4.implication: Evaluate the complete response, from detecting a failure to reaching the machine’s safe state.
sku4.gate: Simulation of fault detection does not establish product certification or system-level safety.
sku4.valueTitle: A datapath fault reaches the gate driver without firmware.
sku4.gateTitle: 39 cycles is a simulation result, not an ISO 26262 certificate.

sku5.headline: SKU-5 carries RS-485 and 8 Mbps CAN-FD on one transceiver, with a ±15 kV pin-protection target.
sku5.context: SKU-5 targets the wired interfaces used across industrial and vehicle equipment, combining bus functions on one part.
sku5.implication: Start with the installed equipment and the replacement requirements; compatibility determines the opportunity.
sku5.gate: Electrical protection, wiring limits and interchangeability still require validation.
sku5.valueTitle: One part covers both RS-485 and CAN-FD buses.
sku5.gateTitle: ±15 kV protection and 1.2 km RS-485 runs need tests on real wiring.

sku6.headline: SKU-6 watches four supply rails and latches a fault after an 8 µs deglitch.
sku6.context: SKU-6 watches supply conditions and records a fault so the wider system can respond. It targets a function needed across many boards.
sku6.implication: Define which power disturbances should stop the system and which should be tolerated.
sku6.gate: The response must be tested against real supply noise and the intended screening requirements.
sku6.valueTitle: Four rails share one latched FAULT_N; the board decides what each fault stops.
sku6.gateTitle: The 8 µs deglitch has to be proven against the board’s own supply noise.

sku7.headline: SKU-7 sweeps 4 GHz at 77 GHz for 3.75 cm range resolution and tracks up to 64 targets.
sku7.context: SKU-7 separates radio-frequency sensing from digital processing, targeting radar functions for vehicles and other platforms.
sku7.implication: Choose the detection task, operating environment and required range before selecting a radar architecture.
sku7.gate: The radio and processing combination must be proven together in the intended scene.
sku7.valueTitle: Two dies: SiGe for 77 GHz RF, 130 nm CMOS for range, Doppler and tracking.
sku7.gateTitle: The SiGe front end has no FPGA equivalent; only silicon proves it.

sku8.headline: SKU-8 drives 1280 columns at up to 12 V and flags a frozen image within two frames.
sku8.context: SKU-8 targets rugged displays, combining panel-driving functions with detection of a frozen image.
sku8.implication: Evaluate readability and failure indication as part of the operator’s task, not simply as display specifications.
sku8.gate: Panel compatibility, environmental performance and fault indication need system tests.
sku8.valueTitle: A frozen image raises an alert within two frames.
sku8.gateTitle: Readability and the freeze alert need tests on the target panel.

sku9.headline: SKU-9 switches 16 smart fuses and routes eight CAN-FD buses inside one vehicle zone.
sku9.context: SKU-9 combines network and power-distribution functions within a vehicle zone; the central vehicle computer remains separate.
sku9.implication: Assess the loads, network traffic and failure isolation of a specific zone before considering consolidation.
sku9.gate: Network timing, power protection and the vehicle safety case remain adoption gates.
sku9.valueTitle: Gateway, fuses and safety island share one zone; central compute stays separate.
sku9.gateTitle: Brake-message latency and fuse trips are proven in the vehicle, not on the chip.

sku10.headline: DG32-Max checks signed firmware in 309 ms from reset, on a lockstep RISC-V pair.
sku10.context: DG32-Max targets imported secure microcontrollers and the separate security chip often used to check firmware before it runs.
sku10.implication: The opportunity is simpler secure control for industrial, drone and EV equipment, provided customer requirements can be met.
sku10.gate: Customer design wins and validation remain essential; the documented design status is not qualified production.
sku10.valueTitle: One chip replaces an imported secure MCU and its separate boot-check chip.
sku10.gateTitle: RTL is feature-complete as of 1 October 2026; no silicon result yet.

sku11.headline: SKU-11 runs a 4–100 kB battery-health model beside four hardwired protection trips.
sku11.context: SKU-11 brings control, battery-health estimation and authentication together. The cell-measuring and isolation components remain external.
sku11.implication: The adoption decision depends on the measurement partner and battery data, as well as the controller itself.
sku11.gate: The Blueprint leaves the measurement partner and field dataset as key dependencies; no manufacturing shuttle is assigned.
sku11.valueTitle: Battery health runs on-chip; cell measurement and isolation stay with a partner.
sku11.gateTitle: The measurement partner and field battery data are not yet chosen.

d100.headline: D100 is a 28 nm drone SoC with its own ₹50 Cr round, raised after mature-node revenue.
d100.context: D100 proposes an Indian flight-control and navigation chip, with a failsafe function that remains separate from higher-level computing.
d100.implication: The Blueprint places it outside the FY31 portfolio revenue plan and proposes a separate ₹50 Cr round after mature-node revenue.
d100.gate: The advanced-process development cost and aviation qualification path remain major delivery gates.
d100.valueTitle: D100 is funded after the eleven mature-node chips earn revenue.
d100.gateTitle: 28 nm development cost and drone qualification set the D100 case.
